expectation: Cytoplasmic stain of branched or dendritic macrophages, monocytes and DCs. Common in gut lamina propria: scattered single cells filling villus cores and the mucosa under the epithelium. Absent from epithelium and lumen.
observed: A: yellow cells are concentrated in the villus/lamina propria cores along the mucosa, not the outline or the lumen. B: a cluster of branched cells next to an unstained epithelial band. C: one cell. D: dendritic cytoplasmic cells. E: a dense branched network that mostly overlaps CD163 (white) plus IBA1-only cells.
why: Branched cytoplasmic cells fill the lamina propria cores and are absent from the epithelium, and they co-localise with CD163 as the subset relation predicts.
notes: IBA1 marks branched myeloid cells packed into the villus lamina propria across the whole section, with clean epithelium. In E most CD163+ cells are also IBA1+, and extra IBA1-only cells fit CD163 being a subset.
